title: Little Girls Wiser Than Men
text:
It was an early Easter, and the snow was melting. Two little girls from neighboring houses, Malasha and Akulya, came out into the lane in their new holiday frocks and found a big puddle. They took off their shoes and started to wade, warning each other to be careful. But Malasha stepped down hard, and the water splashed all over Akulya's new frock.

Akulya ran crying to her mother, who came out and slapped Malasha. Malasha's mother rushed out to defend her daughter, and the two women began to shout at each other. Their husbands came out, then other neighbors, and soon half the village was in the lane, shoving and shouting, ready to fight. An old grandmother tried to calm them, reminding them it was Easter, but no one listened.

Meanwhile the two little girls had forgotten all about the frock. Akulya wiped it as well as she could, and the two of them were back at the puddle. They scratched a little channel with a chip of wood to let the water run off down the lane, and sent a stick sailing along it, right through the legs of the shouting crowd.

The old woman pointed at them. The children had already made up and were playing happily together, while the grown men and women were still fighting about them. The people looked, felt ashamed, laughed at themselves, and went home.
lesson: Children forgive and move on quickly, and adults can learn from them. Ask whether a quarrel is still about the original problem or only about pride.
people: Malasha, Akulya, their mothers, an old grandmother, the villagers
source: Leo Tolstoy, Little Girls Wiser Than Men (1885)
